{
  "decisions": [
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0011",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Reports measured financing and resilience outcomes: inflation-linked sovereign yields rose 80 basis points; portfolio outflows were offset by domestic institutional investors; the peso remained stable amid tightening; and reserves remained adequate at 125 percent of the IMF ARA metric. It attributes stability partly to fiscal fundamentals, monetary commitment to price stability, remittances, and a government foreign-exchange purchase used for public-sector debt amortization.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0010", "U0012"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0012",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.4", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Contains measured credit and financial-system outcomes, including recovering private credit, a capital adequacy ratio above 19 percent versus 16 percent before the pandemic, and ample liquidity at large banks. It also identifies executed anti-inflation actions: fuel-price stabilization with higher-than-budgeted subsidies, a six-month nonbinding food-price agreement, temporary food-tariff reductions, distribution-cost measures, and production support focused on small farmers. PEMEX earnings and production changes provide additional state-enterprise and fiscal-risk evidence.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0011", "U0013", "U0019", "U0020"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0013",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Documents PEMEX debt, supplier obligations, borrowing spreads, capital expenditure, and debt amortization. It gives concrete 2023 budget allocations and fiscal estimates: a deficit increase from 3.8 to 4.1 percent of GDP, an approximately neutral stance, higher interest costs, social pensions, priority infrastructure, fertilizer and rural-support programs, and continued tax-evasion and avoidance efforts. It also records projected growth and employment deceleration under external and domestic tightening.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0012", "U0014"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0014",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.4", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Provides conditional inflation, interest-rate, growth, and potential-output projections, including an assumed policy rate near 10 percent, inflation returning to target around mid-2024, medium-term growth near 2 percent without significant structural reforms, and per-capita potential growth only slightly above 1 percent. It also quantifies external-shock exposure and identifies policy uncertainty and tighter financing as constraints on investment and durable prosperity.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0013", "U0015", "U0016", "U0017"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0015",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.4", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Identifies concrete downside and upside qualifications for Mexico's trajectory: pandemic scarring, policy uncertainty, climate damage, stranded energy assets, inequality and declining incomes, nearshoring, trade diversion, and U.S. spillovers. It also records authorities' growth and inflation forecasts and their attribution of prospective disinflation to supply normalization, fuel-price measures, and monetary policy.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0014", "U0016"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0016",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Supplies a defined IMF G20MOD DSGE simulation method and quantified shock results. A 10 percent oil-price and 50 percent food-price shock raises Mexican inflation nearly 1 percentage point above baseline; adding expectations dislocation and monetary tightening lowers output more than 1 percent below baseline; adding a 1 percent domestic-demand decline pushes output more than 2 percent below baseline. The chunk explicitly notes that a capital-flow shock is not modeled, an important qualification.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0014", "U0015", "U0017"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0017",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.2", "5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Records Banxico's executed monetary response: successive and increasingly large rate increases since June 2021 brought the ex ante real policy rate to about 4 percent by September 2022. IMF staff assesses the response as appropriately calibrated to inflation surprises and delayed convergence, identifies a policy rate of at least 10 percent as likely necessary, and details uncertainty and shock channels relevant to evaluating the response and central-bank operational performance.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0016", "U0018"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0018",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.2", "5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Contains an empirical and risk-based case for further monetary tightening, including Phillips-curve estimates, asymmetric inflation risks, minimum-wage pass-through, and a projected real ex ante policy-rate peak above 5 percent. It also documents transparency actions by Banxico—updated inflation forecasts with every decision since August 2021 and forward guidance—and identifies additional publication and framework-review steps that could improve accountability and adaptive policymaking.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0017", "U0019"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0019",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Provides concrete costs, incidence, and outcomes of anti-inflation fiscal policy. Largely untargeted subsidies were expected to cost about 2 percent of GDP; fuel-price stabilization lowered inflation by an estimated 2 percentage points at a cost near 1.5 percent of GDP, disproportionately benefited higher-income households, and weakened demand-adjustment signals. Food measures had minimal direct inflation impact. The chunk also reports pension and minimum-wage increases, about 5 percent year-on-year growth in real per-capita labor income by mid-2022, and the contrary risk that continued wage increases could add inflation pressure and reduce formal employment among lower-income workers.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0012", "U0018", "U0020"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    {
      "chunk_id": "U0020",
      "include": true,
      "question_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "relevance": "Records authorities' attribution of smooth market adjustment to strengthened monetary communication and their commitment to assess additional communication tools. It gives their stated rationale for fuel stabilization and agricultural/basic-goods measures, including support for underserved farming communities and expected yield effects. It also presents IMF findings on limited countercyclical room under the balanced-budget and debt rules, recommends replacing broad fuel support with targeted safety-net assistance, and quantifies regressive incidence: the top income quintile accounted for about 45 percent of fuel-excise payments versus 6 percent for the bottom quintile.",
      "adjacent_context": ["U0019", "U0021"],
      "exclusion_reason": null
    }
  ]
}
